# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section B continued | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**4:1** And-concerning [...] one-should-not bring dogs into the holy camp, for they might-eat some of-the-bones from the san[ctuary...]

**4:2** [...] with the flesh still on-them. For the dogs [...] the bones and-the-flesh [...]

**4:3** [...] and-they would-defile the camp of-holiness [...] for Jerusalem is the camp of-holiness [...]

**4:4** [...] it is the place which He-chose from-all the tribes of-Israel [...]

**4:5** [...] it is the head of-the-camps of-Israel [...]

**4:6** And-concerning [...] a man should-not [...] a woman [...] who-is-fit for-him [...] for [...] holy seed [...]

**4:7** [...] it is written: you-shall-not sow your field with-two-kinds-of-seed. And-concerning [...] Israel is holy [...]

**4:8** [...] and-it is written concerning-him: you-shall-not let-your-animal mate with-a-different-kind [...]

**4:9** [...] and-not wear a garment of-two-kinds-of-thread [...] and-not bring [...] an-ox and-a-donkey together [...]

**4:10** And-concerning the blind who-cannot see so-as to-be-wary of-any-mixture: and-he-who-cannot see the mixture of-a-transgression —

**4:11** [...] and-concerning the pure [...] the blind cannot discern between the holy and-the-profane [...]

**4:12** [...] they are not able to-see [...] and-therefore they-should-not approach the purity of-the-temple [...]

**4:13** [...] for [...] the one-who-cannot-see is like the one-who-walks in-darkness [...]

**4:14** [...] and-he transgresses without knowledge [...]

**4:15** And-concerning the deaf who-have-not heard the statutes and-the-judgments and-the-purity-regulations, and-have-not heard the ordinances of-Israel —

**4:16** for he-who has-not seen and-has-not heard does-not know how to-practice the law. Yet these approach the purity of-the-temple!

**4:17** [...] and-they touch the purity of-the-temple [...] and-they are not careful [...]

**4:18** [...] for [...] no one who-is-blind or-deaf should-enter the temple [...]

**4:19** [...] for [...] he cannot practice the law and-he defiles the purity [...]

**4:20** And-concerning streams of-liquid: we say that-they have no purity; and-also streams of-liquid cannot separate the unclean from the clean,

**4:21** for the liquid of-streams and-that-which-receives-them is one moisture — one liquid.

**4:22** And-one-should-not bring into the holy camp [...] any [...] that is unclean [...]

**4:23** [...] for [...] the holy camp [...] the dwelling of-His-presence is in-its-midst [...]

**4:24** [...] and-concerning these matters we-have-written to-you, for [...] we-consider them for-your-good [...]

**4:25** [...] and-for the good of-your-people [...] for we saw in-you understanding and-knowledge of-the-Torah [...]

---

*EMET notes: Section B continues with halakhic disputes. The dog prohibition (4:1–5) reflects concern that dogs scavenging sanctuary bones would defile the holy camp, identified with Jerusalem. The mixed-seed/mixed-kind rulings (4:6–9) extend kilayim (mixture prohibitions) to intermarriage, citing Deut 22:9–11 and Lev 19:19. The blind and deaf exclusions (4:10–19) are among the most distinctive and controversial rulings — the blind cannot distinguish mixtures, the deaf cannot learn statutes, so both are barred from temple purity. The liquid-streams ruling (nitsok, 4:20–21) concerns whether a poured stream connects clean and unclean vessels — the sectarians say it does, contra the Pharisees. Hyphenated forms preserve Hebrew construct syntax throughout.*
